metadata.title: Third‑Party Privileged Access

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing and constraining privileged access by vendors, contractors, and third‑party service providers without granting trust or authority.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Identity systems, privileged access management, remote access, support channels, and service connectivity mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Solution pattern governing third‑party privileged access under Zero Trust principles.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines third‑party identities, access approvals, session records, and audit evidence as trust‑relevant data.

props.name: nist-controls
props.remarks: Third‑Party Privileged Access implements identification, access control, and accountability controls.

metadata.remarks: Third‑Party Privileged Access governs how external parties access systems, environments, and services. Granting access does not imply trust, safety, vendor approval, or permission to deploy or execute software.

components.title: Third‑Party Identity Establishment
components.description: Establishes unique, non‑shared identities for third‑party personnel and systems requiring access.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.remarks: Use of compromised or misused third‑party credentials.

components.title: Third‑Party Privileged Access Authorization
components.description: Explicitly authorizes scoped and time‑bound privileged access for third‑party identities.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.remarks: Abuse of excessive or persistent third‑party privileges.

components.title: Third‑Party Session Control and Monitoring
components.description: Monitors, records, and constrains third‑party privileged sessions for accountability and incident response.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.remarks: Abuse of remote access channels by third parties.

techniques.name: Session Logging
techniques.remarks: Recording and monitoring of privileged sessions.

components.title: Third‑Party Access Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Defines what third‑party access does not grant or imply.
components.remarks: Third‑party privileged access does not imply vendor trust, software approval, deployment permission, safety certification, or runtime execution authority.
